result.summary: The street features a residential row on one side and a large facility with a long blank wall on the other. While sidewalks are present, the environment lacks marked crossings and lane markings, creating a wide, undefined roadway that may encourage higher vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: There are no designated or painted areas for pedestrians to cross the wide roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the center of the roadway

hazards.name: Blank frontage
hazards.description: A long windowless wall on the left side reduces natural surveillance and pedestrian comfort.

hazards.name: Wide, unmarked roadway
hazards.description: The absence of lane markings on a wide street can encourage higher vehicle speeds and unpredictable driving behavior.

interventions.title: High-visibility crosswalks
interventions.description: Install painted crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian crossing points and improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb extensions
interventions.description: Implement bulb-outs at intersections to reduce crossing distance and slow turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Street trees
interventions.description: Plant trees along the sidewalk to provide a buffer from traffic and improve the aesthetic quality of the blank wall.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street with a wide, paved sidewalk directly adjacent to a multi-unit building. Pedestrian safety is compromised by multiple driveway curb cuts for garages and a lack of physical buffer between the walkway and the roadway.

hazards.name: Driveway conflict points
hazards.description: Two garage entrances require vehicles to cross the sidewalk, creating potential conflict points with pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Ground floor of the brick building

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars along the curb can block sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers in the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image where the grey SUV is parked

hazards.name: Degraded road surface
hazards.description: Significant cracking in the asphalt roadway may pose a hazard for pedestrians crossing or for other road users.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Buffer Zone
interventions.description: Introduce a planting strip or furniture zone between the sidewalk and the curb to provide physical separation from traffic.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility at potential crossing points.

interventions.title: Roadway Resurfacing
interventions.description: Repair the cracked asphalt to provide a smoother and safer surface for all road users.

result.summary: The environment is a wide, multi-lane arterial road adjacent to an elevated highway structure, creating a high-speed and somewhat hostile pedestrian experience. While basic infrastructure like sidewalks, marked crosswalks, and signals are present, the long crossing distances and industrial frontage reduce overall safety and comfort.

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The width of the roadway requires pedestrians to be exposed to traffic for a significant duration without a refuge island.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: A large trailer parked on the right and the pillars of the elevated highway obstruct sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement
hazards.description: Cracking and wear in the asphalt surface can create trip hazards or uneven footing for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median or refuge island to break up the long crossing distance and provide a safe waiting area.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Add bulb-outs at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Enhanced Lighting
interventions.description: Improve street lighting, particularly under the elevated highway structure, to increase visibility and perceived safety.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is located beneath an elevated highway structure, creating a dark and shadowed walkway. While a wide sidewalk is present, the area is dominated by industrial land use, large commercial vehicles, and a lack of clearly marked pedestrian crossings.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Large Vehicles
hazards.description: A large box truck parked under the bridge obscures sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and vehicles approaching from the background.

hazards.name: Poor Visibility under Infrastructure
hazards.description: The elevated highway creates deep shadows, reducing the visibility of pedestrians to drivers, especially during transition periods of light.
hazards.location_in_image: The entire area beneath the bridge deck

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossing
hazards.description: There is no marked pedestrian crossing at the transition point between the foreground street and the area under the bridge, despite the presence of a sidewalk.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install a continental-style marked crosswalk to clearly define the pedestrian path across the roadway.

interventions.title: Under-Bridge Lighting
interventions.description: Install supplemental pedestrian-scale lighting underneath the highway structure to eliminate dark spots and improve personal security.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions to reduce the crossing distance and prevent large vehicles from parking too close to the crossing point, improving sightlines.
